whatThisFileIs: An R1 authorship claim for the AFC-274 hardening of scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh: a THIRD path list, NEVER_EXIST_PATHS, refused in both modes so scripts/grep-awareness-write-context.sh cannot be committed at all rather than merely reported untracked. Coder is the author. R2 does not machine-apply -- scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh is not on REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS, which names services/directus/schema/engine/**, services/directus/schema/migrations/**, tests/db/**, scripts/retention-literal-gate.sh and scripts/r2-grandfathered.json, and never scripts/ as a whole -- so the claim registry is recorded here for attribution and for the review record, not to clear a gate. The CTO reviews Coder compliance-path commits; the verdict is recorded below when it lands.
basis: THE RESIDUAL. scripts/grep-awareness-write-context.sh is the superseded 183-line predecessor of scripts/retention-literal-gate.sh (288 lines). It carries a header reading 'AFC retention-literal gate', so in a diff it presents AS the gate rather than as a dead copy, but its file filter is `-name '*.ts' -o -name '*.js' -o -name '*.vue'` and it never opens a .sql file: it would have missed the retention engine entirely, which is the one thing the live gate exists to scan. No reference to it exists under .github/ or scripts/, so nothing ever invoked it -- pure hazard, a control-shaped file rather than a weaker control. The CTO deleted it; it REGENERATED in the shared tree, which is why deletion alone was never the fix. GUARDED_PATHS catches it only while it is untracked, staged or modified. The dangerous route is `git add` then `git commit`: the tree goes clean, the dirty half has nothing to report, and review_required() is silent too, because the path is not on R2 -- nothing on it is meant to exist, so there is nothing to review. MEASURED on the committed guard in a scratch repository, not argued: that exact commit exited 0. WHAT THIS ADDS. (1) NEVER_EXIST_PATHS plus never_exist(), a third list kept separate from GUARDED_PATHS ('dirty here is unshippable') and from REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS ('clean here still needs a named reviewer'); this one means 'this path is not a thing that exists'. It is not merged into either: merging it into R2 would let a claim plus a reviewer launder a file that must not exist at all, and merging it into GUARDED_PATHS silently degrades it back to 'untracked is bad', which is the route that just failed. never_exist() is exact string equality on purpose, so one entry cannot refuse a whole subtree. (2) check_commit(): the refusal runs BEFORE the R2 `continue`, in its own accumulator (deny_rc), so the closing prose names the rule that actually fired -- a denylist-only failure no longer ends with 'a compliance-path commit has no registered claim or no named reviewer', which would be output disagreeing with the fact it reports. prov_rc carries R1/R2 and wins on exit 2, so an unreadable claim file is not downgraded by an unrelated hit. (3) guard(): the same refusal on the working-tree side, collected BEFORE the 'clean' early-return, because a tree that is clean and still holds the file is the one state neither existing list can report on; the dirt prose is suppressed when there is no dirt. (4) The question in check_commit() is 'does the path exist in this commit's TREE', not 'was it touched': `git diff-tree --name-only` reports a DELETION as a touched path, and refusing the deletion would refuse the only action that clears the state. (5) assertions 12a-12e in --self-test. The header's CONTRACT and its new THREE LISTS section document the third rule and the fact that the three are three different rules, not three scopes of one.
verificationRecorded: MEASURED on a scratch clone of this repository at HEAD and on a scratch fixture repository, before and after. --self-test: original 40 ok / 0 FAIL / exit 0; this change 45 ok / 0 FAIL / exit 0 (12a never_exist matches the seeded path only and R2 still does not cover it; 12b a commit ADDING the path exits 1, names it, and carries no R1 or R2 verdict; 12c a commit touching a DIFFERENT scripts/ path with the same empty trailers still exits 0, so 'refuse every scripts/ commit' cannot pass 12b; 12d a CLEAN tree holding the path is refused by guard() and passes again once it is gone; 12e the commit that DELETES the path is not refused). A/B on an identical fixture add-commit: the guard at HEAD exits 0 (the hole), this change exits 1 with the refusal; on the matching delete-commit both exit 0. Full history, `--check-commit HEAD`: both exit 1 -- the verdict does not change, the only output difference is the new refusal naming 1f43c9e, the root commit that first added the file (bb50b4b later deleted it and is correctly NOT refused). merge-in-gate.sh --self-test exits 0, and it embeds this guard. `bash scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh` on the real tree exits 1 and now names scripts/grep-awareness-write-context.sh under 'a path that must never exist is present in the tree' alongside the ten pre-existing dirty violations from other agents' in-flight work. GUARDED_PATHS and REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS are byte-identical to HEAD: no scope change, no path added to R2, no claim, review record or grandfather entry touched or created. No migration, no engine change, no role or privilege change, no personal data: the CTO migration-approval path is not engaged. scripts/grep-awareness-write-context.sh itself was NOT deleted by this run -- it is not mine to attribute or remove, it is left exactly where it is, and the guard now names it as forbidden rather than merely untracked.
